concerns.text: T026 is listed twice (Phase 4 and Phase 5) and remains unimplemented (`[ ]`). It consumes `data/processed/mapped_data.parquet` (produced by T019.2). The duplicate listing creates ambiguity in the execution order, and the unimplemented status breaks the producer-consumer chain for FR-012 (KEGG mapping) required by US3 validation tasks (T033, T034).

T009.1.1, T009.1.2, and T009.2 are marked `[ ]` (unimplemented). These tasks produce the external dataset artifacts required by T012 (RealAdapter) and T030 (LODO validation). Without these producers, the consumer tasks in US1 and US3 cannot execute, violating the foundational data-flow dependency.

T007.1 (Checksum verification) is marked `[ ]`. Constitution Principle III mandates checksumming of all generated data before downstream use. T007 (Generator) produces the primary artifact, but T007.1 (the consumer of that artifact for hashing) is missing, breaking the data hygiene flow required before T015 (Preprocessing) can safely consume the data.

T009.3.1 (Validation of distinct stress_vector_seeds) is marked `[ ]`. T030 (LODO validation) explicitly depends on this verification to ensure dataset independence (FR-010). The consumer (T030) cannot safely proceed without the producer (T009.3.1) confirming the distinct seeds.

T040.1 (Generate quickstart.md) is marked `[ ]` and listed as depending on T046. However, T042 (Execute quickstart.md) depends on T040.1. This creates a circular or blocked flow where the documentation generation is incomplete, preventing the final validation task (T042) from running. The ordering is logically sound but the unimplemented status blocks the end-to-end flow.
